title: Yakitori
subtitle: Japanese grilled chicken skewers with a sweet soy glaze
excerpt: Yakitori are small grilled chicken skewers coated in a sticky tare glaze. The glaze is a simple mix of soy, mirin, sake, and honey that reduces and caramelises in the oven or under the grill.
sourceNotes: Yakitori, meaning 'grilled bird', became a staple of Japanese izakaya bars in the Edo period. Charcoal grilling is traditional but a hot oven or grill works well at home.

recipe.batchNotes: Marinate larger quantities in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Skewer and cook in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tare glaze keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks. Make a double batch and use it for other grilled meats.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 200C / Gas 7. Or use the grill on high.

content.text: If using wooden skewers, soak them in cold water for 30 minutes before threading the chicken. This stops them scorching in the oven.
Combine all the tare glaze ingredients in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from the heat and cool.
Put the chicken chunks in a bowl. Pour over half the glaze and mix well to coat. Cover and leave in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven. Thread the chicken onto skewers, alternating with pieces of spring onion.
Lay the skewers in the roasting tin. Roast for 10 minutes.
Brush with the remaining glaze. Return to the oven for another 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the glaze is sticky and caramelised.

items.symptom: The glaze is burning before the chicken is cooked through.
items.cause: The oven temperature was too high or the glaze was applied too early.
items.fix: Apply final glaze only in the last 8 minutes of cooking.

items.cause: Thighs were overcooked; the cut is forgiving but not indefinitely.
items.fix: Check after 18 minutes total; pull as soon as juices run clear.
